data.title: Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom – Hrádok, a hillfort with a medieval tower
data.excerpt: On the andesite crag of Hrádok, on the boundary between Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom and Bystričany, the Lusatian people built a hillfort around the 1st millennium BC; two lines of ramparts with pincer-shaped gateways still encircle its upper plateau. The people of the Púchov culture rebuilt it, the Slavs occupied it in the 9th century, and in the middle of the enclosure the foundations of a stone tower 9.5 × 9.8 m in size – probably of the 13th century – were uncovered.
data.metaTitle: Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom – the Hrádok hillfort
data.metaDescription: The Hrádok hillfort between Kamenec and Bystričany was built by the Lusatian people around the 1st millennium BC and later rebuilt by the Púchov culture.

keyFacts.label: Location
keyFacts.value: The hillfort lies on the upper plateau of the andesite crag of Hrádok (spot height 880, or 661), about 6 km south-east of the village of Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom.

keyFacts.label: Fortification
keyFacts.value: The upper plateau is encircled by two lines of ramparts, with entrance gateways of the pincer-shaped type in the north-western and south-eastern parts of the outer rampart.

keyFacts.label: Donjon
keyFacts.value: In the middle of the fortified area the foundations of a squarish stone building measuring 9.5 × 9.8 m were uncovered, which served as a dwelling and at the same time a watchtower.

keyFacts.label: Local name
keyFacts.value: The inhabitants of the village of Bystričany still call the whole rock with the donjon Dvorčená skala.

keyFacts.label: Construction of the ramparts
keyFacts.value: The second trench uncovered a continuous layer of charcoal and burnt timber, which suggests ramparts of drystone-laid stones with a timber chambered construction.

keyFacts.label: Traces of Roman influence
keyFacts.value: The sherd material obtained at Hrádok contains, alongside elements of the earlier phase of the Púchov culture, also elements that may possibly be assigned to the period of the Roman provinces.

keyFacts.label: Prehistoric occupation
keyFacts.value: A large quantity of sherd material from the Celtic-Dacian-Púchov occupation, as well as from the earlier Hallstatt period, was found in the vicinity of the hillfort.

children.text: Evidence of occupation of the area of present-day Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom, and of the village of Bystričany, dates as far back as the period of the Lusatian culture. On the boundary between these two villages, around the 1st millennium BC, the Lusatian people built a hillfort – Hrádok, which served as a refuge and a hiding place from enemies. The hillfort was later rebuilt by the people of the Púchov culture. The life of the inhabitants was also influenced by the Celtic-Dacian tribes, because they taught them to mine and work iron ore, to use the potter’s wheel and to ride a horse. In the vicinity of the hillfort a large quantity of sherd material from the period of the Celtic-Dacian-Púchov occupation (2nd century BC – 2nd century AD) was found, as well as from the earlier Hallstatt period. In the 9th century the Slavs appear at the hillfort. In the period of Great Moravia fortifications were renewed or newly built at strategic places. For this reason the hillfort in present-day Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom was also rebuilt and used. After the break-up of Great Moravia, developments in the Upper Nitra region can hardly be mapped and can rather only be assumed in the context of other historical events.

children.text: The hillfort is situated on the upper plateau of the andesite crag of Hrádok (spot height 880, or 661), about 6 km south-east of the village of Kamenec pod Vtáčnikom. The andesite spur, meander-shaped, is inaccessible from the western and southern sides. On the other sides the upper plateau is encircled by two lines of ramparts. In the north-western and south-eastern parts of the outer rampart, gateways into the fortified enclosure were recorded. We assign them to gateways of the pincer-shaped type.

During the excavation the foundations of a medieval feature (a donjon) in the middle of the fortified area were uncovered, and two trenches also established the structure and the chronological position of the hillfort itself. The trenches cut across the outer rampart, on its north-western (trench no. 1) and south-eastern (trench no. 2) arc. Trench no. 1 succeeded in recording part of the faced wall of the entrance gateway, where there was a thick layer of destruction.

In the second trench, which was also sunk at the place of the presumed entrance gateway no. 2, a continuous layer of charcoal and burnt timber was found over a short stretch, which allows us to assume at this site ramparts of drystone-laid stones with a timber chambered construction between them. In the trenches and on the area of the hillfort enclosed by the ramparts a large quantity of sherd material was found, indicating the beginning of occupation at Hrádok in the Hallstatt period, the intensification of occupation in the Celtic-Dacian-Púchov period and a phase of Slavic occupation in the 9th century. The latest is the feature whose stone foundations were uncovered in the central part of the fortified area of the hillfort, probably belonging to the 13th century. It is a squarish stone building measuring 9.5 × 9.8 m, which evidently served as a dwelling and at the same time a watchtower. The inhabitants of the village of Bystričany still call the whole rock on which the donjon stands Dvorčená skala. (information obtained directly from a local Rusalka)

children.text: The sherd material obtained from trenches 1 and 2 was probably for the most part already in a secondary position. The stratigraphy recorded in the section of the trenches provided no basis for determining the individual building, and hence chronological, phases of the creation of the ramparts. The structure and overall character of the inner rampart enclosing a small space are not yet known, which is a frequent phenomenon precisely at Púchov hillforts. The sherd material obtained at Hrádok is very important, because besides material characteristic of the earlier phase of the Púchov culture it also contains elements that may possibly be assigned to the period of the Roman provinces.
